newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: N.Korea and S.Korea Red Cross heads meet.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea and S.Korea Red Cross heads meet.

text.p: North and South Korean Red Cross society officials have met ahead of a donors' meeting to discuss the logistics of stepping up aid to the famine-hit North, a spokeswoman for the world relief body said on Tuesday.

The talks were held on Monday in Geneva, where the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) will present an expanded appeal for the communist North to officials from 15 donor societies on Thursday and Friday.

Paik Yong Ho, secretary-general of the North Korean Red Cross, and Kim Heh Nam, director of international relations at the South Korean Red Cross, met at Federation headquarters, according to spokeswoman Marie-Francoise Borel.
North Korea desperately needs large-scale food aid to avert famine caused by years of economic decline and two years of devastating floods, according to international aid agencies.
Paik is heading a two-member delegation from Pyongyang, according to a spokesman at the North Korean diplomatic mission to the United Nations European headquarters in Geneva.
"The situation in my country is very critical now," the mission's spokesman said.

"We are still in urgent need of a large amount of assistance from the outside world," he added. "We expect the meeting this week would lead to further assistance from (Red Cross and Red Crescent) national societies."

Under the first direct pact between the Red Cross societies of rival North and South in more than a decade, representatives signed an agreement in Beijing on May 26 on the delivery of some 50,000 tonnes of food, mainly corn, from Seoul to Pyongyang.
